activities.title: स्वास्थ्य शिविर
activities.description:
*"आरोग्यम" शिविर*

रोटरी क्लब का ऑफ बदायूं सेंट्रलद्वारा एक निशुल्क चिकित्सा जांच शिविर "आरोग्यम" दिनांक 26 - 07- 2024 दिन शुक्रवार को प्रातः 10 बजे से 12 बजे तक नवयुवक इंटर कॉलेज स्कूल के विशाल प्रांगण में आयोजित किया गया।

इस शिविर में कक्षा 5से 6तक के 210छात्र - छात्राओं के दांतों व आंखों का परीक्षण किया गया।
हीमोग्लोबिन टैस्ट भी किया गया।
छात्राओं के वजन तथा लंबाई का माप भी किया गया।
इस कार्यक्रम को सफल बनाने में नवयुवक स्कूल की प्रधानाचार्य जी का तथा स्टाफ का सराहनीय सहयोग रहा।
बदायूं शहर के प्रमुख दंत विशेषज्ञ डॉक्टर चित्रांश सक्सेनl डॉक्टर गोपाल वैश्य डॉ नरेंद्र डॉक्टर एके शर्मा जी का विशेष सहयोग रहा ,हीमोग्लोबिन व छात्राओं की लंबाई व वजन माप में क्लब के सचिव डॉक्टर संजीव गुप्ता व उनके स्टाफ का विशेष सहयोग रहा
रोटरी क्लब आफ बदायूं सेंट्रल के अध्यक्ष अनिल गुप्ता ने सभी डॉक्टर वह स्कूल के स्टाफ का बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद प्रदान किया
स्वल्पाहार सभी स्टाफ व क्लब के सदस्यों को कराया गया
क्लब के अन्य सदस्यों में श्री विपिन अग्रवाल दीपक सक्सेना मुनेंद्र कुमार सिंह संजय रस्तोगी कुलदीप रस्तोगी प्रमोद शर्मा सुरजीत गुप्ता डॉक्टर कौशल गुप्ता गोपाल रस्तोगी राम मोहन अग्रवाल अनिल गुप्ता सीमेंट प्रदीप गुप्ता सोनू गुप्ता रविंद्र गुप्ता रितेश गुप्ता सदस्यों ने भाग लिया अंत में असिस्टेंट गवर्नर श्री सुरेंद्र चाणक्य जी ने सभी का धन्यवाद दिया

activities.description:
The “Arogyam" Free Mega Health Checkup Camp,” organized by [Rotary Club Of Aligarh Friends], was a comprehensive health initiative aimed at providing accessible and free medical screenings in Schools .The camp offered a range of health services to 7200 students, addressing key health concerns and promoting overall wellness.

Provide free Eye checkup, Dental checkup, Height & Weight.
Raise awareness about preventive health measures and early detection of diseases.
Offer personalized health advice and referrals for further care as needed.
We organised this camp from 15-07-24 to 31-07-24

activities.description: 78 बच्चे ऐसे पाए गए जिनकी आंखें बहुत ज्यादा कमजोर थी और जिसका उन्हें व उनके माता पिता को जानकारी भी नही थी। कुछ बच्चों के दातों में परेशानी थी। कुछ बच्चों का वजन बहुत कम था। कुछ बच्चों का वजन थोड़ा ज्यादा था। इसी प्रकार की थोड़ी समस्याएं जो इस उमर के बच्चों में प्रायः पाई जाति है वही सब देखने को मिली।

activities.title: आरोग्यम (Health Checkup)
activities.description:
रो डा भरत खेडिया ने सभी बच्चों चेकअप किया तथा बच्चों को हरी सब्जी खाने के लाभ बताए तथा खाने के लिए प्रेरित किया।
अध्यक्ष डा राजीव भारती ने बच्चों को ज्यादा मोबाइल उपयोग से बचने की सलाह दी।
दातों की डा पल्लवी त्रिपाठी ने बच्चों को 2 बार ब्रश अर्थात सोने से पहले ब्रश करने के महत्व को बताया।

activities.title: आरोग्यम
activities.description:
छात्राओं के स्वास्थ की स्क्रीनिंग डॉक्टर्स की टीम ने की 
स्वास्थ्य परीक्षण में मुख्य रूप से लंबाई, वजन, पेट में कीडे, आंखों की जांच तथा दातों का परीक्षण किया गया।

activities.description:
The eve of 1st July 2024 witnessed the Grand Installation ceremony of Rotary Club Mathura Central District 3110. The auditorium echoed with applause for our Multitalented and Philanthropist DG Rtn Mr Neerav Nimesh Agrawal and his Spouse Rtn Ruchi Agrawal. The presence of PDG DRFC Zone 6 Rtn Sharat Chandra ji and his better half Mrs Anjana ji added an aura of joy in the ceremony.
Our club was honoured to have PDG Rtn Ravi Prakash Agrawal ji and PDG Rtn Kishore Katru ji who shared their valuable inputs with all the Rotarians. 
DGE Rtn Rajendra Vidyarthi ji along with his wife Mrs Shalini Vidyarthi ji ,DGN Rtn Jasbir Bhatia ji and his wife Mrs Daljeet Bhatia ji ,and ADG Rtn Ashish Sahu ji marked the occasion with their esteemed presence. 
President Rtn Rohit Kapoor and Secretary Rtn Mrs Deepti Tentiwala along with senior Rotarians of the club welcomed all the dignitaries. 
It was a seamless, inspiring and value added ceremony where the youngsters Ms Vanya Tentiwala and Ms Reet Agrawal along with Rtn Pratibha Agrawal carried out their duties effortlessly as MOCs.
The Event was followed by Fellowship and Dinner.

activities.title: Arogyam Mega Health Check Up Camp
activities.description:
Rotary District 3110's mega health project Aarogyam under the aegis of Rotary Club Mathura Central organized several health screening camps in various schools. From July 9, 2024, to July 13, 2024, a Kids Health Camp was conducted from 9 AM to 1:30 PM. This program included dental checkups, eye examinations, hemoglobin tests, and other health-related activities, during which approximately 4,342 children from 10 schools were screened by doctors from Mathura. The camp was inaugurated by the Rotary Mathura Central's esteemed DG, Rtn. Neerav Nimesh. All Rotarians actively participated in various camps, boosting the morale of the children.

The camps were organized under the supervision of senior Rotarians Rtn. B.B. Kalra, Rtn. J.K. Katara, Rtn. Ajit Agarwal, Rtn. Naresh Berman, Rtn. K.D. Agarwal, Rtn. Ashok Agarwal, Rtn. Umesh Goyal, Rtn. K.M. Khandelwal, and Rtn. Dushyant Agarwal. Rtn. Ashutosh Kumar, Rtn. Neelesh Tentiwala, Rtn. Ashutosh Garg, Rtn. Dr. Vartika Kishore, Rtn. Neha Agarwal, Rtn. Aarti Kapoor, Rtn. Ruchi Agarwal, Rtn. Shweta Khandelwal, Rtn. Anuradha Shukla, Priya Maheshwari, and Rtn. Ashima Khandelwal also actively participated in the event.

The President of Rotary Club Mathura Central, Rtn. CA Rohit Kapoor, Club Secretary Rtn. Deepti Tentiwala, and Joint Secretary Rtn. Dr. Roli Bansal, along with the doctors from K.D. Dental College, made valuable contributions to the smooth execution of the health screening camps, which was highly commendable. The schools where the “Aarogyam” camps were held are as follows:

Chameli Devi Khandelwal Girls Inter College, Mathura

activities.title: Meet with Everester Nisha
activities.description:
It was a privilege to meet, greet and felicitate an inspiring personality Ms Nisha Kumari and her Coach Mr. Nilesh Barot. Nisha is not an ordinary girl…She has conquered the peaks of Mount Everest inspite of all the odds and is amongst the few who have achieved this feat. Her journey of adventures has inspired her to add another feather to her cap. Famous as Everester Nisha started on Cycle from Vadodra Gujrat to travel on her bicycle till London. At an age of 30 years Nisha n her supporting coach Mr Nilesh have together embarked on this tedious journey. They reached Mathura on the eve of 13th July 2024 and it was wonderful to have lunch with her hearing to her stories of capturing the peaks of Mount Everest. Our best wishes to both of them in their endeavours.
In the ceremony Rtn B B Kalra, President Rtn.CA Rohit Kapoor, Rtn.Neelesh Tentiwala, Apoorv Agrawal, Ashutosh Shukla, First lady of District Ruchi Agrawal, Secretary Rtn.Deepti Tentiwala,Joint Secretary Dr. Roli Bansal and Shweta Khandelwal was present.

activities.title: Miyawaki Plantation
activities.description:
Rotary Club of Agra Royal organized a workshop on Miyawaki afforestation method while planting trees.

“Let's come together to plant trees – from beneath our feet, and around the world.”


This was the statement of Dr. Akira Miyawaki who gave the technique to develop urban forest in small space while promoting urban afforestation. Around the world, Miyawaki warriors carry out large-scale reforestation campaigns, carrying forward the important work started half a century ago.
Rotary Club of Agra Royal along with one such Miyawaki warrior Mrs. Ritu Khandelwal organized a workshop on Miyawaki afforestation method and conducted tree plantation to develop the forest. Mrs. Ritu Khandelwal has already developed two Miyawaki forests and she gave detailed information to everyone about it. President SangIta Aggarwal welcomed everyone and said that to secure the life of the coming generations, we will have to do massive tree plantation today. For which Miyawaki technique is very effective. Chief guest District Governor Rtn. Nirav Nimesh Aggarwal stressed on developing more Miyawaki forests in the District by adopting this technology. Distinguished guest Rotary Coordinator Sharat Chandra praised the service work being done by Rotary Club of Agra Royal.

activities.title: Swalpahaar: Remembering Our Late Charter President
activities.description: On July 8, 2024, the Rotary Club Brahmavarta Kanpur organized a heartfelt service activity named "Swalpahaar" at Snehalay, Shayam Nagar, Kanpur, in honor of late charter president. The event aimed to commemorate his legacy through a meaningful initiative to feed approximately 150 mentally challenged and handicapped individuals. The ceremony commenced with the lighting of a diya and a reverent worship of Lord Ganesh. Rotary members paid homage to their late charter president with a poignant tribute, observing a solemn 2-minute silence and adorning his photograph with flowers. Under the guidance of Project Director- Rtn. Anil Dadu, President- Rtn. Manoj Pandey, Secretary- Rtn. Ashish Agarwal, and Treasurer- Rtn. K.K. Agarwal, the Rotary Club members distributed food boxes to the attendees. This act of service not only provided nourishment but also honored the memory of our esteemed leader, reflecting the Rotary Clubs commitment to community welfare and remembrance.

activities.title: Hariyali Teej Mahotsava
activities.description: Hariyali Teej is a vibrant and significant festival women celebrate in various parts of India, particularly in the northern states. It marks the beginning of the monsoon season and honors the divine union of Goddess Parvati and Lord Shiva. This joyous occasion is characterized by traditional rituals, colorful attire, and cultural festivities.Hariyali Teej festival 2024 holds great religious and cultural significance. It commemorates the reunion of Goddess Parvati with Lord Shiva after years of penance and devotion. This festival symbolizes the strength and purity of marital bonds and is a day for married women to seek blessings for a happy and prosperous married life. It also marks the arrival of the monsoon season, which brings renewed hope and prosperity to the land.

activities.title: Aarogyam Day - 1
activities.description:
Rotary Club of Kanpur Divinity successfully completed its Day - 1 of Aarogyam Mega Health Check-up Camp at Onkareshwar Saraswati Vidhya Niketan Inter College.

activities.title: Mango Party
activities.description:
The Mango Party was held on:

Date: July 17, 2024
Time: 08:00 PM
Venue: Hotel Royal Residency, G.T. Road, Aligarh

The event was graced by the presence of numerous Rotarians, their families, and special guests. The primary objective of the event was to foster camaraderie among members and celebrate the summer season with the king of fruits – the mango.

Welcome Address:
The event commenced with a warm welcome address by the President of the Rotary Club of Aligarh, Rajeev Agarwal ‘Raymond’. In his speech, he expressed heartfelt gratitude to all attendees for their enthusiastic participation and support. He emphasized the importance of such gatherings in strengthening the bonds within the Rotary community.

Activities and Highlights:
1. Mango Tasting Session: The highlight of the evening was the mango tasting session, where a variety of mangoes were showcased. Attendees had the opportunity to taste different types of mangoes, each with its unique flavor and texture.
2. Games and Competitions: The event featured several fun-filled games and competitions, including a mango eating contest, mango carving competition, and a quiz on mango trivia. These activities added an element of excitement and engagement to the event.
3. Cultural Performances: The evening was enlivened by cultural performances, including traditional dances and music. These performances not only entertained the guests but also showcased the rich cultural heritage of the region.
4. Networking and Fellowship: The Mango Party provided an excellent platform for networking and fellowship among Rotarians. Members had the chance to interact, share experiences, and discuss future projects and initiatives.

Acknowledgements:
In his closing remarks, President Rajeev Agarwal ‘Raymond’ once again thanked everyone for their presence and participation. He acknowledged the efforts of the organizing committee and volunteers who worked tirelessly to make the event a grand success. He also expressed his appreciation for the sponsors and partners who supported the event.

Impact and Feedback:
The Mango Party was well-received by all attendees, who appreciated the opportunity to relax, enjoy, and connect with fellow Rotarians. The event successfully achieved its objective of fostering a sense of community and camaraderie. Feedback from participants was overwhelmingly positive, with many expressing their eagerness to attend similar events in the future.

Conclusion:
The Mango Party hosted by the Rotary Club of Aligarh was a memorable event that brought together members and their families for an evening of fun, food, and fellowship. It not only celebrated the joy of summer but also reinforced the spirit of unity and togetherness within the Rotary community. The success of this event sets a positive precedent for future gatherings and initiatives.

activities.title: 75th Installation Ceremony
activities.description:
Date: 14 August, 2024
Time: 8:00 PM
Venue: Hotel Royal Residency, G.T. Road, Aligarh

Overview:
The Rotary Club of Aligarh celebrated its 75th Installation Ceremony. The event marked a significant milestone in the club’s history, reflecting its enduring commitment to community service and leadership.

Event Details:
The ceremony commenced promptly at 8:00 AM, with Rotarians and distinguished guests gathering to witness the installation of new officers and the induction of new members. The atmosphere was filled with enthusiasm and a sense of accomplishment as the club prepared to embark on another year of impactful service.

Distinguished Guests:
The event was graced by several notable dignitaries, including the Mayor of Aligarh, who delivered an inspiring speech on the importance of community service. Additionally, more than six past district governors, the District Governor (DG) elect, the DG nominee, and the current DG were present, adding to the event’s prestige and significance.

Induction of New Members:
One of the highlights of the ceremony was the induction of more than 16 new members into the Rotary Club of Aligarh.

Programs Planned for the Current Session:
The newly installed officers and members outlined an ambitious and comprehensive plan for the current session. 

Ceremony Highlights
The ceremony was meticulously planned and executed, ensuring a memorable experience for all attendees. Key highlights included:
• Opening Remarks: The event began with a welcome address by the outgoing president, who reflected on the club’s achievements over the past year and expressed gratitude to all members for their dedication and support.
• Installation of New Officers: The installation of new officers was conducted with great pomp and ceremony. The incoming president took the oath of office, pledging to uphold the values and mission of Rotary. The new board of directors was also introduced and installed.
• Guest Speeches: The Mayor of Aligarh and the past district governors delivered motivational speeches, emphasizing the importance of Rotary’s work and encouraging members to continue their efforts in serving the community.
• Awards and Recognitions: Several members were recognized for their outstanding contributions to the club and the community. Awards were presented for various categories, including community service, leadership, and membership growth.
• Cultural Performances: The ceremony featured cultural performances by local artists, adding a festive touch to the event. The performances were well-received and added to the overall celebratory atmosphere.
• Networking and Fellowship: The event provided an excellent opportunity for networking and fellowship among members and guests. The interactions fostered a sense of camaraderie and strengthened the bonds within the Rotary community.

Conclusion
The 75th Installation Ceremony of the Rotary Club of Aligarh was a resounding success, reflecting the club’s unwavering commitment to service and leadership. The event not only celebrated past achievements but also set the stage for future initiatives aimed at making a positive impact on the community. The presence of distinguished guests and the induction of new members underscored the club’s growing influence and the increasing interest in its mission.
As the Rotary Club of Aligarh embarks on a new session, it remains dedicated to its core values of service, fellowship, diversity, integrity, and leadership. The planned programs for the current session promise to address critical community needs and contribute to the overall well-being of society. With the continued support and active participation of its members, the Rotary Club of Aligarh is poised to achieve even greater heights in the years to come.

activities.description:
DETAILED REPORTS FOR EACH EVENT IN AUG 2024

Rotary Club Agra Grace, in collaboration with Rotary Club Agra Taj City, organized an Inter-School Quiz Competition at Ujala Cygnus Rainbow Hospital. Students from five schools including Shivalik Public School, St. Conrad's Inter College, Holy Public School, Dr. MPS World School, and Shivalik Cambridge College participated. The competition had an exciting quiz round with visuals, photos, and videos. St. Conrad's students claimed first place, followed by Holy Public School and Shivalik Cambridge College. Certificates, medals, and shields were awarded to winners, and saplings were gifted to the participants and parents as a symbol of growth and knowledge.

activities.title: Tree Plantation
activities.description: A massive tree plantation program was organized this morning on 11th August 2024 by the members of Rotary Club Agra Royal in the Khelgaon complex of Dayalbagh. 101 saplings were planted by the club in the campus. President Sangita Aggarwal welcomed everyone and said that to secure the lives of the coming generations, we will have to plant trees extensively today.

activities.title: Installation of soft water purification plant & Water Cooler
activities.description: Soft water purification plant & Water Cooler provided by Vacmet India Limited CSR fund was installed by Rotary Club of Agra Royal in Chandra Balika Vidyapeeth Inter College, New Agra. President Sangita Agarwal welcomed all the guests and explained that the lack of clean potable water is one of the world's biggest health problems – and Rotary under its WASH programs is mobilizing resources and investing in infrastructure and training to provide clean water to everyoneChief guest, District Governor Nirav Nimesh Aggarwal inaugurated the plant and also called upon the teachers of this school to join the teacher training program of Rotary. He laid emphasis on self-defense and self-reliance while giving career related guidance to the girl students.

activities.title: Independence Day
activities.description: Rotary Club of Agra Royal celebrated the 78th Independence Day with flag hoisting and national anthem at Chandra Balika Vidyapeeth Inter College, New Agra. Various cultural programs were presented by the school students in this function. President Sangita Agarwal, while welcoming all the guests, called upon the school students that we have to understand the responsibility towards our country India and work hard to make our country even stronger and prosperous. School manager Sameer Gupta Vibhav told about the sacrifices of freedom fighters and also appealed to the girls that they can create their independent identity in the society only by getting educated

activities.title: 3rd Charter Day
activities.description: Rotary Club of Agra Royal celebrated its third Charter day at Hotel Lemon Tree. The chief guest at the program was senior doctor Dr. Anjana Pandey Gupta. While inaugurating the program, President Sangita Agarwal told that the club has been continuously working for the needy in the field of education, health and environment and has achieved a leading position in the District through its service work. Secretary Srishti Jain gave details of the work done by the club. The history of the club was told by Charter President Sharda Gupta.

activities.title: Flag Exchange
activities.description: Rotary Club of Agra Royal welcomed Rotarian Uday Kumar, International Director and Public Image Chair of Rotary Club of Bengaluru Agara (District 3191). Flag Exchange was done with Rotarian Uday Kumar by Club President Rotarian Sangita Agarwal at the event organized at Khelgaon Sports Complex. Aparna Poddar, Meera Gupta, Sanjana Sharma, Ruby Aggarwal and Rekha Kapoor were present in the program

activities.title: Nandotsav
activities.description: The Rotary Club of Agra Royal and Rotary Club Agra came together in a grand celebration of Lord Krishna's birth, marking the festive occasion of Nandotsav with immense enthusiasm and joy. The event, held at The Outhouse Club, Vibhav Nagar, was a vibrant showcase of devotion and unity as members from both clubs staged five enchanting episodes, or leelas, from Lord Krishna’s life: His Birth, Nandotsav, Makhan Chori (butter stealing), the battle with Kalia Naag, and the divine Maha Raas. Each of these mesmerizing performances left the audience in awe, as they vividly brought to life the magic and spiritual essence of Krishna’s journey.

activities.title: " 78वा स्वाधीनता दिवस उत्सव "

सर्वप्रथम अध्यक्ष रो.डॉ रमेश गुलाटी,सचिव (मेजर डोनर) रो.श्रीकृष्ण खेतान,निवर्तमान अध्यक्ष रो. योगेंद्र मोहता,अध्यक्ष निर्वाचित रो. सतीश गोयल,क्लब ट्रेनर रो. ओ पी सलूजा रो. डॉ एम सी गुप्ता द्वारा संयुक्त रूप से पॉल पी हैरिस तथा भारत माता के चित्र पर माल्यार्पण कर दीप प्रज्वलित किया गया।तत्पश्चात ध्वजारोहण हुआ।
सभी के द्वारा राष्ट्र-गान हुआ।रो.आर सी नरूला द्वारा संचालन किया गया।स्वल्पाहार का सभी ने आनंद लिया।

activities.title: स्वतंत्रता दिवस

पूरा देश 78वें स्वतंत्रता दिवस का जश्न मना रहा है। इस अवसर पर तिरंगा फहराते हुए देखना, चाहे वह लाल किले पर हो, राज्यों की राजधानियों में हो या स्थानीय इलाकों में, हमेशा हमारे दिलों को रोमांचित करता है।रोटरी क्लब उन्नाव सिटी ने आशा सुपर स्पेशलिटी हॉस्पिटल उन्नाव में झंडा रोहन कर स्वतंत्रता दिवस हॉस्पिटल के मरीज एवं स्टाफ के साथ बड़े हर्ष उल्लास मनाया।
कार्यक्रम सफल बनाने में अध्यक्ष राजीव भारती, रो डा भूपेंद्र सिंह, वरिष्ठ सदस्य रो दिनेश चंद्र जैन, कोषाध्यक्ष रो विशाल चंद्र गुप्ता, उपाध्यक्ष रो महेश गुप्ता, रो अरविंद गुप्ता, रो मयूर गुप्ता, रो अमित आनंद, रो रंजीत कुशवाहा आदि उपस्थित रहेl

activities.title: पौधा रोपण

दिनांक 22 अगस्त 2024 पौधा रोपण का कार्यक्रम श्री जगदम्बा प्रसाद स्मारक इंटर कॉलेज राजेपुर उन्नाव में संपन्न हुआ।

activities.title: Janmashtami Celebration 🎉🎉
activities.description:
The pious festival of Janmashtami is the much awaited festival as the whole club participates with full zest. This year too Rotary Club of Mathura Central celebrated Krishna Janmashtami on the eve of 21st August. The event was loaded with various mesmerising dance performances by the children and lady Rotarians of the club and entertaining games. The venue echoed with Cheers n chants of “Jai Kanhaiya Lal ki , Haathi Ghoda Palki” as Laddoo Gopal was brought in and placed on his Aasan. The Arti was followed by soulful Bhajans and Dahi Handi. All the veteran Rotarians and young members participated with full energy in the games organised by the Team. It is during these gatherings when the generation gap disappears and members of all age groups come together as a family to celebrate and enjoy.
The beautiful evening ended with mouth watering Chaat and traditional Indian dinner and beautiful return gifts and Of course with Loads of blessings from Lord Krishna !

The protest witnessed the silent rage of all the women of all age groups against this barbarism. Rtn Ruchi Agrawal, Rtn Shweta Khandelwal Rtn Ashima Khandelwal along with young Rotractor Shinjini Bansal lead the peaceful march with the hope in hearts that Strict laws are framed and executed against the crimes committed towards women.

activities.title: Installation
activities.description:
अपने क्लब के ६१वे अधिष्ठापन समारोह में आये सभी मेंबर्स व परिवार को हम आभार व्यक्त करते है जिन्होने आकर टीम २०२४-२५ का उत्साहवर्धन किया। हम अपने वरिष्टजनों को भी धन्यवाद देते है जिनके मार्गदर्शन से यह कार्यक्रम सफलतापूर्वक संपन्न हुआ। प्रोजेक्ट डायरेक्टर्स रोटेरियन कुलभूषण मक्कड़ जी,प्रशांत गुप्ता जी,संकल्प भल्ला जी व राजिंदर सिंह जी को भी धन्यवाद। विशेष आभार MOC रोटेरियन स्वतंत्र सिंह जी का जिन्होंने दिन रात एक करके रिकार्ड समय में क्लब की मैगजीन को इतनी सुंदरता से प्रिंट करवाया व मंच संचालन किया।रो संतोष गुप्ता जी,रो पंकज गुप्ता जी,रो शुभांक गुप्ता ,रो श्वेता भल्ला जी, रो सीमा वर्मा जी,रो ऋचा पोरवल जी, एस डी वर्मा जी, ऐन रुचि सेठ जी को भी आभार जिन्होंने एंट्री से लेकर बैक स्टेज की व्यवस्था सुचारू रूप से करने में अपना सहयोग दिया।रो हेमंत सजनानी जी को अपने मुख्य अतिथि श्री विनोद बंसल जी को दिन में कानपुर के धार्मिक स्थलों में लेकर जाने के लिए भी धन्यवाद।विशेष आभार रोटेरियन सुभाष खेड़िया जी का जिनके प्रयास से हमे इतने अच्छे वक्ता श्री बंसल जी को सुनने का अवसर मिला।
रो यजुवेंद्र सिंह जी को प्रिंट मीडिया में अधिष्ठापन समारोह का इतना अच्छा कवरेज कराने के लिए भी धन्यवाद।
अंत में आप सभी को पुनः हृदय से नमन व धन्यवाद एवं आशा करते है कि आप सभी मेंबर्स पूरे वर्ष सभी कार्यक्रमों में आते रहेंगे।

activities.title: Sanjha Chula - Nishulka Rasoi Ghar
activities.description:
The Sanjha Chula Community Service Program, an initiative by our Rotary Club, aimed to provide gas stoves and gas cylinders to the kitchen of Gandhi Eye Hospital. This project was designed to enhance the cooking facilities at the hospital's kitchen and ensure a safe and efficient cooking environment for the staff and patients.

Project Details:

Objective: To improve the kitchen facilities at Gandhi Eye Hospital by providing modern cooking equipment.
Implementation: The Rotary Club funded the purchase of gas stoves and gas cylinders, which were installed in the hospital's kitchen by a professional team.
Impact: The new cooking equipment has streamlined the cooking process at the hospital, allowing the staff to prepare meals more efficiently. This has positively impacted the overall operations of the hospital.
Funding: The Sanjha Chula Community Service Program was fully funded by our Rotary Club through contributions from members and fundraising events. The club's generous support made this project possible and contributed to the well-being of the hospital staff and patients.

Conclusion: The Sanjha Chula Community Service Program exemplifies our commitment to serving the community and making a positive difference in the lives of others. We are grateful for the opportunity to support Gandhi Eye Hospital through this project and look forward to continuing our efforts to uplift and empower those in need.

activities.title: Moksha Dham
activities.description:
Project Overview: Rotary Moksha Dham is an ongoing project initiated by Rotary Club Aligarh with the aim of creating a serene and environmentally friendly space for the community. This project focuses on beautifying and maintaining a designated area for relaxation and reflection, accessible to all residents of Aligarh.

Project Details:

Objective: To develop a tranquil space within the city for individuals to unwind, meditate, and connect with nature.
Implementation: The project involved landscaping, planting trees and flowers, installing benches, and creating walking paths in Rotary Moksha Dham. Regular maintenance and cleanliness drives are conducted to ensure the upkeep of the area.
Impact: Rotary Moksha Dham has become a popular spot for residents to find solace amidst the hustle and bustle of city life. The greenery, peaceful ambiance, and well-maintained facilities have garnered positive feedback from the community.
Sustainability:

Rotary Club Aligarh is committed to the long-term sustainability of Rotary Moksha Dham. Regular community engagement activities, awareness campaigns on environmental conservation, and tree plantation drives are organized to promote environmental stewardship.
The club collaborates with local authorities and environmental organizations to ensure the continued success and sustainability of the project.
Future Plans:

Rotary Club Aligarh aims to further enhance Rotary Moksha Dham by introducing additional amenities such as water features, solar lighting, and recreational facilities.
The club plans to organize community events, workshops, and awareness programs in Rotary Moksha Dham to promote wellness, environmental consciousness, and community cohesion.
Conclusion: Rotary Moksha Dham stands as a testament to Rotary Club Aligarh's dedication to creating inclusive and sustainable community spaces. The project has provided a sanctuary for residents to connect with nature, relax, and rejuvenate. As the project continues to evolve, the club remains committed to fostering a sense of belonging and harmony within the community through Rotary Moksha Dham.

We extend our gratitude to all members, partners, and volunteers who have contributed to the success of Rotary Moksha Dham.

activities.title: Girls Stiching & Embroidery Training Centre
activities.description:
The Rotary Stitching & Embroidery Training Centre commenced its operations on 20th June 2022, offering a comprehensive training program in stitching and embroidery. The center is equipped with 25 Singer machines, each designed for various stitching and embroidery operations.

The training program features a minimum 6-month diploma course, providing students with a strong foundation in stitching and embroidery skills. Upon completion of the diploma course, some students have the option to extend their training based on their learning objectives. Presently, the center has 24 students actively engaged in the program.

In the academic year 2022-23, 9 students successfully completed the diploma course and were awarded their diplomas, showcasing their proficiency in stitching and embroidery. Over the last two years, the training center has enrolled a total of 34 students, indicating a growing interest in the courses offered.

A notable achievement of the program is that 4 students have purchased sewing machines for home use, leveraging their skills to pursue stitching and embroidery as a professional career. This demonstrates the practicality and effectiveness of the training provided at the Rotary Stitching & Embroidery Training Centre.

activities.title: Medical Camp For Jail Inmates
activities.description:
Agra, July 1, 2024 — The Rotary Club of Agra marked the beginning of the Rotary New Year with a comprehensive health check-up camp at the District Jail Agra. This initiative aligns with the Rotary International's focus on Maternity and Child Health month. The camp aimed to ensure the well-being of female inmates and their children residing with them by addressing their health concerns.
A team of esteemed doctors offered their services for this noble cause:
• Rotarian Dr. Alok Mittal – ENT Specialist
• Dr. Atul Bansal – Child Specialist
• Dr. Arushi Bansal – Gynaecologist
• Dr. Nitin Mahajan – Dentist
• Dr. Sonika Mahajan – Dentist
• Rotarian Dr. Rahul Singh – Eye Specialist
• Dr. Amit Gaur – General Physician
During the camp, free oral medicines, eye drops, ear drops, syrups, dental creams, and eyeglasses were distributed to the inmates after thorough examinations by the experts. A total of 300 inmates, including children and some male inmates, were examined.
Coinciding with CA & Doctors' Day, the club honored the participating doctors with mementos. CA Rotarian Udit Bansal was also recognized for his contributions. Jail Superintendent Mr. Hariom Sharma joined Club President Rotarian Namrata Panicker, Secretary Er. Ashish Agarwal, and senior club members in the felicitation ceremony.
The cooperation from the jail authorities was commendable, ensuring the smooth execution of the camp. Rotarian Namrata Panicker expressed gratitude to the jail authorities for allowing the club to serve the inmates and their children.
Senior members present at the camp included Rotarian Vishnu Saran Mehra, Rotarian Ashish Agarwal, Rotarian Jitendra Jain, Rotarian Manoj R. Kumar, Rotarian Vinod Gupta, Rotarian Sangita Agarwal, Rotarian Rekha Kapoor, Rotarian Srishti Jain, Rotarian Sunil Kapoor, Rotarian Sanjeev Agarwal, Rotarian Radhey Shyam Sharma, Rotarian Sanjana Sharma, and Rotarian Aradhana Gupta.
This initiative reflects the Rotary Club of Agra's commitment to serving the community and addressing essential health needs.

activities.title: Aarogyam Health Mission 1
activities.description: The District Governor of Rotary International District 3110, Neerav Nimesh Agrawal, set a target to conduct health check-ups for 120,000 children in Rotary District 3110 from July 1st to July 21st. Responding to this call, the Rotary Club of Agra held a health check-up camp at Sacred Mother Junior School in Kamla Nagar, Agra, from 9 AM to 11 AM. Students from class 2 to class 8 received dental, hemoglobin, and eye exams from Dr. Manoj Jain (Senior Pediatrician), Dr. Vijay Singh (Pediatrician), Dr. Rahul Singh (Ophthalmologist), and Dr. Ankit Gupta (Dentist). The doctors examined 200 students today. Program coordinator Dr. Alok Mittal mentioned that the mission aims to gather data to inform the state government about children's health. Club President Namrata Panicker stated plans to check around 3,000 children in various city schools. Secretary Ashish Agrawal thanked the school management, and the club honored the doctors with mementos. Vice President Jitendra Jain, Ashish Agrawal, Rajiv Lochan Bhardwaj, Manoj R. Kumar, Vinod Gupta, and others contributed significantly to the event's success.

activities.title: Aarogyam Health Mission 2
activities.description:
Rotary District 3110 has embarked on an ambitious project under its Aarogyam Mission to conduct health screenings for 120,000 students. The primary goal of these health check-up camps is to identify and diagnose early-stage ailments in students, which are often overlooked by parents.
In line with this mission, Rotary Club of Agra organized a health screening camp today at Ganeshram Nagar Saraswati Shishu Balika Vidhya Mandir, Balkeshwar, Agra. During the camp, 800 students underwent comprehensive health check-ups. Senior Pediatricians Dr. Manoj Jain and Dr. Sashi Mauli examined the students for general health issues, Eye Specialist Rotarian Dr. Rahul Singh addressed vision-related problems, and Dr. Ankit Gupta provided dental assessments. The screenings revealed that many students had undiagnosed issues such as weak eyesight and low hemoglobin levels.
Rotary Club of Agra President Rotarian Namrata Panicker emphasized the mission's objective to detect and address health issues in students from grades three to eight, which are often neglected and can be managed effectively if caught early. Club Treasurer Rotarian CA Udit Bansal expressed gratitude to the school management for their excellent arrangements for the camp. School Manager Smt. Shruti Singhal reaffirmed the institution's commitment to student welfare, while School Principal Smt. Charu Patel thanked the Rotary Club for their ongoing support.
Mission Director Rotarian Dr. Alok Mittal announced that these health camps will continue until July 21, 2024. Rotary Club of Agra members, including Rotarian Tulika Bansal, Rotarian Sanjeev Agarwal, Rotarian Manoj R. Kumar, Rotarian Sunil Kapoor, Past President Rotarian Ashish Agarwal, Immediate Past President Rotarian Rajesh Jain, and Rotarian Mukesh Chaturvedi, were present to assist the doctors. Smt. Durgesh Sharma and Smt. Rashmi Agarwal managed the arrangements on behalf of the school management.

activities.title: Aarogyam Health Mission 3
activities.description:
As part of the Rotary District 3110's ongoing Aarogyam Health Mission, the Rotary Club of Agra organized a comprehensive health check-up camp at Ramswaroop Singhal Girls Inter College, Daresi Road, Agra. This initiative targeted students from classes fifth to eighth, aiming to promote health and wellness among young learners.
The camp saw a remarkable turnout with 398 students undergoing screenings for vision, dental, and general health issues. The dedicated team of professionals ensured thorough examinations:
• Dental Check-up: Dr. Deepak Kurup, Dr. Sristhi Kurup, and Dr. Malti Sagar
• General Check-up: Gynecologists Dr. Jolly Goyal and Dr. Smita Nagar
• Eye Check-up: Supervised by Rotarian Dr. Rahul Singh
The findings highlighted prevalent issues such as oral hygiene problems, poor vision, and low hemoglobin levels among many students. The club members also measured the height and weight of the students for further health assessments.
The Principal of Ramswaroop Singhal Girls Inter College, Smt. Kumud Grover, expressed heartfelt gratitude to the Rotary Club of Agra for their commitment to the well-being of the children. She praised the club's efforts in organizing such an impactful event.
The camp was conducted under the expert guidance of District Mission Director, Rotarian Dr. Alok Mittal. Rotary Club of Agra President, Rotarian Namrata Panicker, expressed appreciation to the medical professionals by presenting mementos as tokens of gratitude for their selfless service. Vice President - Rotarian Jitendra Jain, Director - Rotarian Sunil Kapoor, Executive Secretary – Rotarian Manoj R. Kumar took care of the arrangements in the camp.

activities.title: Aarogyam Health Mission 4
activities.description:
As part of the ongoing health check-up mission by District 3110 – Aarogyam, a comprehensive health camp was held today at Queen Victoria Girls’ Inter College, Agra. Preliminary screenings for height, weight, and eye health were conducted by class teachers beforehand.
Senior Gynaecologist Dr. Pooja Agarwal, along with Gynaecologist Dr. Prachi Agarwal, addressed haemoglobin deficiencies and other general health concerns among the children. Dental issues were expertly handled by Dr. Deepak Kurup, Dr. Srishti Kurup, and Dr. Malti Sagar. Eye examinations were conducted under the supervision of Rotarian Dr. Rahul Singh. In total, 364 children benefited from the camp's services.
Club President Rotarian Namrata Panicker, Secretary Rotarian Eng. Ashish Agarwal, and Mission Director Rotarian Dr. Alok Mittal honored the doctors for their invaluable contribution. School Principal Mrs. Joyas Sylas expressed heartfelt gratitude to the Rotary Club members for organizing this essential health camp.
The event saw active participation from Rotarians Amit Sisodia, Shalini Agarwal, Radhey Shyam Sharma, Rotarian Sanjeev Agarwal, Rotarian Jitendra Jain, Rotarian Sunil Kapoor and Rotarian Manoj R. Kumar.

activities.title: Aarogyam Health Mission 5
activities.description:
As part of the ongoing Arogyam Project initiated by District Governor Rotarian Neerav Nimesh Agarwal, the Rotary Club of Agra organized a comprehensive health check-up camp today for the junior section students at Ganeshram Nagar Saraswati Shishu Balika Vidhya Mandir in Balkeshwar.
489 students from classes third, fourth, and fifth were screened for eye, haemoglobin, dental, and general health issues. Senior Child Specialist Dr. Manoj Jain and Paediatrician Dr. Shashi Mauli Singh focused on detecting haemoglobin deficiencies and addressing general medical concerns. Dental health was overseen by Dr. Ankit Gupta and Dr. Mohit Gupta, while Dr. Rahul Singh and his team managed eye-related examinations.
Club President Rotarian Namrata Panicker expressed gratitude to the doctors and the school management for their continuous support of the Aarogyam Health Mission. Mission Chairman Dr. Alok Mittal honored the attending doctors with mementoes in recognition of their contributions.
School Principal Smt. Charu Patel and Head Mistress Smt. Rashmi Agarwal thanked the Rotary Club members for organizing the camp for their students. The event was successfully coordinated by Rotarians Jitendra Jain, Sunil Kapoor, and Manoj R. Kumar, ensuring smooth arrangements throughout the day.

activities.title: Aarogyam Health Mission - 6
activities.description: Under the Arogyaam Health Mission initiated by Rotary District 3110, Rotary Club of Agra conducted another health check-up of 235 students of classes 3 to 8 at Midas Academy, Sikandra. In the health check-up camp, paediatrician Dr. Vijay Singh examined the children for haemoglobin and other problems. Dental problems were examined by Dr. Yatendra Dagur, while the children's eyes were examined under the supervision of Dr. Rahul Singh. In the health check camp, most of the children were diagnosed with weak eyesight. Mission Chairman Rotarian Dr. Alok Mittal said that due to excessive use of mobile, laptop and TV by children these days, most of the children are weakening their eyesight, of which their parents are unaware. Club President Rotarian Namrata Panicker said that the purpose of these health camps is to identify the basic diseases found in children in the initial stage so that they can be treated well in time. Rotarian Manoj R Kumar, Rotarian Ritu Nandan Singh, Rotarian Shailendra Nath Sharma, and Rotarian Pradeep Mittal made significant contribution in organising the medical camp. School director Mr. Manthan Rawat expressed his gratitude to the doctors present at the camp and the Rotary Club of Agra.

activities.title: Plantation 1 at Body & Soul
activities.description:
With the arrival of the monsoon season, the Rotary Club of Agra has launched its annual plantation program, starting with the planting of 150 saplings at the Body & Soul premises and the adjacent cricket ground. The initiative saw enthusiastic participation from club members, who planted a variety of saplings including Neem, Guava, Jamun, Bakain, Champa, and Gulmohar.
The plantation drive was spearheaded by Rotarian Ram Mohan Kapoor, whose support was instrumental in the successful execution of the event. The activity was followed by a session of poetry recitation and a light breakfast, fostering a sense of community and shared purpose among the participants.
Prominent Rotarians present at the event included Rotarian Ashish Agarwal, Rotarian Sangita Agarwal, Rotarian Jitendra Jain, Rotarian Srishti Jain, Rotarian Dr. Alok Mittal, Rotarian Sunil Kapoor, Rotarian Rekha Kapoor, Rotarian Ritunandan Singh, Rotarian Amit Sisodia, Rotarian Manoj R. Kumar, Rotarian Radhey Shyam Sharma, Rotarian Sanjana Sharma, Rotarian Udit Bansal, Rotarian Vinod Gupta, and Rotarian Aradhana Gupta.
Club President Rotarian Namrata Panicker extended her heartfelt gratitude to all the club members and guests for their invaluable contributions to the plantation camp. She highlighted the importance of such initiatives in enhancing the green cover of the city and promoting environmental sustainability.
The Rotary Club of Agra remains committed to its mission of community service and environmental conservation, with the plantation program marking a significant step towards a greener future.

activities.title: Workshop - Maternal Health, Hygiene & Sanitation
activities.description:
Rotary International observes July as Maternal & Child Health Month. To commemorate this, the Rotary Club of Agra organized a workshop on maternal health at Sacred Mother Junior School, Kamla Nagar, Agra. The keynote speaker for the event was Professor Dr. Ruchika Garg from SN Medical College, Agra, who holds a national record for vaccinating the highest number of medical students against cervical cancer in the country.
Dr. Garg emphasized the importance of a healthy lifestyle, noting that many women today neglect this aspect, leading to numerous health issues. She advocated for a return to traditional practices, underscoring the scientific basis behind them, and cautioned against blindly adopting Western habits. Additionally, Dr. Garg highlighted the benefits of physical exercise for maintaining both mental and physical fitness. Addressing cervical cancer, she urged young mothers to ensure their daughters receive timely vaccinations to prevent future complications. She also provided guidance to the women on maintaining their personal hygiene.
The session was highly interactive, with Dr. Garg addressing various queries from young mothers. Club President Rotarian Namrata Panicker expressed gratitude to Dr. Garg for her valuable insights, emphasizing that mothers need to prioritize their health to better support their families.
Headmistress Mrs. Kritika Tahaliani thanked the Rotary Club of Agra for organizing the workshop for the school's parents. District Chairman of Health Committee – Rotarian Dr. Alok Mittal and Rotarian Manoj R. Kumar, who managed the arrangements, were also present during the workshop.

activities.title: Rotary Junior Ambassador Contest
activities.description:
To inspire the next generation with the spirit of selfless service, the Rotary Club of Agra proudly organized a competition to identify the Rotary Junior Ambassador for 2024, held at The International School, Agra. The event aimed to educate students about Rotary’s noble mission and its unwavering commitment to serving communities worldwide.
Rotarian Namrata Panicker, the club president, emphasized that Rotary’s core philosophy is “Service Above Self.” She highlighted that unlike other student organizations, Rotary International offers young individuals, aged 12 to 18, the unique opportunity to join the Interact Club—a global community dedicated to service. This platform not only connects students with their peers around the world but also deepens their understanding of impactful community service.
She further explained that through Rotary, students can cultivate leadership skills and participate in international programs such as the Rotary Youth Leadership Awards and Rotary Youth Exchange Programs, broadening their horizons and fostering global citizenship.
Past President Rotarian Dr. Alok Mittal shared insights into Rotary’s rich history, which dates back to 1905, and its diverse initiatives, including the monumental global campaign to eradicate polio. Club Learning Facilitator Rotarian Dr. R.L. Bharadwaj introduced the students to Rotary’s guiding principle, the Four-Way Test, which embodies the very essence of the organization.
Following this enlightening session, students were invited to present their ideas on how they could contribute to societal change, competing for the prestigious title of Rotary Junior Ambassador. Aradhita Sharma, a talented student from Class 7, emerged as the winner and was honored with the Rotary Junior Ambassador Trophy.
In a momentous announcement, Rotarian Sanjay Kalra, the school’s managing director, revealed plans to establish an Interact Club at the school, providing students with an invaluable opportunity to connect with the global network of Interactors. School Principal Shri Abhay Mathur expressed heartfelt gratitude to the Rotary Club of Agra for offering their students this enriching experience and deepening their connection with Rotary’s mission. Club Executive Secretary Rotarian Manoj R. Kumar and Youth Service Director Rotarian Vinod Gupta were also present in the program.

activities.title: Blood Donation Camp
activities.description:
The Rotary Club of Agra successfully conducted a blood donation camp at Lokhitam Blood Bank in Kamla Nagar, Agra. The camp was organized with the dual purpose of addressing the critical demand for blood and encouraging the community to contribute to this life-saving cause.
Rotarian Namrata Panicker, Club President, emphasized that while the immediate goal was to meet the urgent need for blood, the broader objective was to inspire people to become regular donors and support blood banks in meeting the increasing demand. "Blood donation is a vital service to society, and we hope this camp motivates more individuals to participate in the future," she remarked.
Community Service Director Rotarian Umesh Gupta highlighted the impact of blood donation, noting that a single unit of blood can save up to three lives. He also reassured the public that donating blood is a safe and healthy activity that every eligible person should consider doing every six months.
Club Secretary Er. Rotarian Ashish Agarwal expressed mixed feelings about the turnout. "Although we anticipated a larger participation, we were heartened by the 17 members who stepped forward to donate. Their contribution is truly commendable and sets a positive example," he said.
Club Treasurer CA Rotarian Udit Bansal extended his heartfelt thanks and appreciation to all members who donated blood during the camp, acknowledging their generosity and commitment to the cause.
The camp saw the active participation of several Rotarians and community members, including Past President Rotarian Ashish Agarwal, Rotarian Dr. Alok Mittal, Rotarian Kamal Agarwal, Rotarian Meera Gupta, Rotarian Sachin Mittal, Rotarian Vijay Singh Pundhir, Rotarian Manoj R. Kumar, Prem Kumar Ravi, Anshu Mittal, Kamini Agarwal, Tripti Singh, Pramesh, and Rotarian Shailendra Nath Sharma, among others.

activities.title: Feel Good Litrecy Kit Distribution
activities.description:
As part of its ongoing commitment to service and community, Rotary Club of Agra is celebrating the Rotary Year 2023-24 as the "Rotary Feel Good Year." The theme highlights the club’s focus on spreading joy and positivity, not only within the Rotary community but also across the broader society. The goal, as Club President Rotarian Namrata Panicker stated, is to ensure that every Rotarian feels proud of being part of one of the oldest and most prestigious Rotary Clubs in India, and to share this happiness by making a tangible difference in the lives of others.

In line with this vision, Rotary Club of Agra today donated 140 'Feel Good Literacy Kits' to students of a government primary school in Mehra Naharganj, Barauli Aheer, Agra. The initiative was aimed at supporting the educational journey of underprivileged children, providing them with essential learning materials for the academic year. The kits, thoughtfully designed, included school bags filled with all-in-one notebooks, drawing books, colored pencils, sharpeners, biscuits, and a dental kit to help children not only learn but also maintain their health and well-being.

Club President Rotarian Namrata Panicker elaborated on the importance of such initiatives, saying, "We have put together these literacy kits to ensure that the basic educational needs of these children are met for the entire year. Over the years, Rotary Club of Agra has focused extensively on basic education and literacy, areas that are critical to improving societal outcomes. Addressing the gaps in education automatically addresses several other issues related to poverty and development."

The club’s International Service Director, Rotarian Sunil Kapoor, emphasized the club’s broader commitment to uplifting the community. “Just last month, we organized health camps to tackle basic health issues faced by school children. Now, through initiatives like these literacy kits, we are taking responsibility for bringing smiles to every child in the city. Our school contact programs aim to make a positive impact on both their health and education.”

The event was graced by Basic Education Officer Shri Mahesh Chandra, who praised Rotary Club of Agra for its consistent efforts to promote health and education. "The work being done by Rotary in these sectors is commendable. It is encouraging to see organizations taking a proactive role in enhancing the lives of children, especially in underserved areas."
Club Joint Secretary Rotarian Nidhi Sharma expressed her gratitude to all the guests and parents who attended the event, acknowledging their support in making the program a success. She also highlighted the collective efforts of Rotarians, parents, and educators in fostering a supportive learning environment for the children.

Rotary Club of Agra’s Executive Secretary Rotarian Manoj R. Kumar & Past President Rotarian Aarti Mehrotra ensured that all the arrangements for the event were meticulously handled, ensuring that the day unfolded seamlessly.

With the 'Feel Good Literacy Kits,' Rotary Club of Agra continues its mission to spread joy, foster education, and make a lasting difference in the lives of children across the city. As the Rotary Year 2023-24 progresses, the club remains dedicated to multiplying happiness by extending its reach and service to even more communities.

activities.title: Plantation 2 at Rawat Farmland
activities.description:
In a commendable effort to contribute towards environmental conservation, the Rotary Club of Agra conducted an extensive plantation drive this morning at two prominent locations in the city: Sector 9 Park, Awas Vikas Colony, and Rawat Farms, Sikandra. The initiative saw enthusiastic participation from local residents, students, and Rotarians, all united in their mission to create a greener and more sustainable environment.
At Sector 9 Park, club members Rotarian Amit Sisodia and Rotarian Ritunandan Singh took the lead by planting 60 saplings with the active support of local residents. As a part of this initiative, an additional 80 saplings were distributed to the community, encouraging people to take an active role in environmental preservation. The involvement of local residents in this initiative highlights the Rotary Club’s commitment to fostering a sense of responsibility and community participation in protecting the environment.
In the second phase of the drive, 100 saplings were planted at Rawat Farms, Sikandra. This effort was carried out in collaboration with students from the Eco Club at Midas Academy, who joined hands with the Rotary Club to further the cause of environmental protection. The participation of students is a promising step towards educating the younger generation about the importance of sustainability and their role in safeguarding nature.
Several prominent Rotarians were present to support the drive, including Rotarian Gunjan Girish Singh, Rotarian Shailendra Nath Sharma, Rotarian Dr. Alok Mittal, Rotarian Sachin Agarwal, Rotarian Raj Mittal, Club Secretary Rotarian Ashish Agarwal, and Rotarian Manoj R. Kumar. Their active participation not only strengthened the initiative but also underscored the Rotary Club’s dedication to environmental causes. Mr. Manthan Rawat, Director of Midas Academy was also present to support his students & the mission.
A wide variety of plants were both distributed and planted during the drive. These included fruit-bearing trees such as Guava, Jamun, Karonda, Lemon, Gooseberry, Jackfruit, and Plum, as well as other species like Neem, Gulmohar, Semal, Imli, Kaith, Arjun, and Kaner. These species were chosen not only for their environmental benefits but also for their role in enhancing biodiversity and supporting local ecosystems.
The plantation drive was part of the Rotary Club of Agra’s ongoing efforts to combat climate change and promote environmental sustainability. By planting trees and involving the community, the club is contributing to the global movement for a cleaner, greener planet.
Through initiatives like this, the Rotary Club of Agra continues to play a pivotal role in addressing the pressing environmental challenges of our time, leaving a lasting impact on both the local community and the environment.

activities.title: Oral Hygiene Workshop
activities.description:
Rotary Club of Agra, continuing its commitment to community service, organized an impactful workshop on handwash techniques, safe drinking water, and oral hygiene for the students of Vivekanand Sarswati Shishu Mandir, Agra Cantt. The workshop, aimed at students from classes second to eighth, underscored the importance of basic hygiene and healthy living.

The event commenced with a warm welcome by the school’s principal, Shri Manendra Tiwari, and the management team, as they graciously received the esteemed members of the Rotary Club. The session opened with an engaging demonstration of handwashing techniques by Rotarian Dr. Rajeev Lochan Bharadwaj. He stressed that clean hands are the first line of defense against illness and encouraged the students to adopt proper handwashing habits to protect their health.

The significance of oral hygiene was brought to light by guest speaker Dr. Sonika Mahajan, who spoke passionately about the role of teeth in eating, talking, and smiling. She highlighted the importance of good dental habits from an early age, emphasizing brushing and flossing twice daily, rinsing after meals, and regular dental check-ups. Dr. Mahajan shared easy-to-follow tips for maintaining oral hygiene and advised the students on what to avoid to keep their teeth healthy and strong.

Following this, Rotarian Gunjan Girish Singh delivered a compelling talk on the critical need for clean drinking water. She emphasized that safe water is not only a basic human right but a vital factor in children’s health and development. With a focus on practicality, she advised families who may not have access to advanced filtration systems to boil water before consumption, thus safeguarding their health from waterborne diseases.

Rotary Club President, Rotarian Namrata Panicker, addressed the gathering with an inspiring message, saying, “Healthy children build a healthy nation.” She passionately expressed the Rotary Club’s long-standing commitment to ensuring the well-being of future generations, citing their 86-year legacy of service in Agra. She highlighted the crucial role of personal hygiene, clean water, and a healthy environment in shaping a nation's future.

The Rotary Club also ensured that the children would be continually reminded of the lessons from the workshop by placing awareness posters around the school premises. To further support their health journey, the club distributed free dental kits and served light refreshments to all participants. The event saw an enthusiastic response from over 250 students, all actively engaged and eager to learn.

Several prominent Rotary members, including Rotarian Shailendra Nath Sharma, Immediate Past President Rotarian Rajesh Jain, and Executive Secretary Rotarian Manoj R Kumar, were present at the workshop, lending their support and reinforcing the club's unwavering dedication to community welfare.

This initiative reflects Rotary Club of Agra's continued efforts to foster awareness and promote healthy habits in young minds, helping to build a stronger, healthier society for tomorrow.

activities.title: Nation Builder Awards
activities.description:
The Rotary Club of Agra has long recognized that teachers are the backbone of a civilized society, playing an essential role in shaping future generations. In line with this belief, the club has been honoring educators for their significant contributions to excellence in education through the prestigious Nation Builder Awards. This year, the club continued its tradition with a grand felicitation ceremony held at Hotel Clarks Shiraz, Agra.
The event commenced with the lighting of the ceremonial lamp, symbolizing knowledge and enlightenment, followed by a graceful classical dance performance of Saraswati Vandana by Miss Raisha Mahajan. Fourteen distinguished teachers, nominated by the Rotary Club of Agra, were honored for their outstanding dedication and efforts in nurturing young minds.
The chief guest for the occasion, Rotarian Neerav Nimesh Agrawal, addressed the gathering, emphasizing the pivotal role teacher’s play in character building and nation-building. He remarked, "Teachers not only contribute to the academic growth of students but also guide society by shaping the values and direction of future generations, making the world a better place to live in."

The educators recognized with the Nation Builder Awards were:
• Miss Neelam Elveena Yunas and Miss Meghna Roberts from Queen Victoria Girls’ Inter College,
• Mrs. Shreya Pathak and Mrs. Richa Massey from St. George’s College,
• Mrs. Meenu Bhandari and Mrs. Almas Thomas from St. Peters College,
• Mrs. Geeti Maheshwari, retired from St. Peters College,
• Mrs. Renu Lal and Mr. Radha Raman from The International School Agra,
• Ms. Alpana Singh and Ms. Mahak Jagotta from St. Conrad’s Inter College,
• Mrs. Anju Mahajan and Ms. Victoria Gomes from St. Patrick’s Junior College.
• Mrs. Arti Hariprasad from St. Clare’s Senior Secondary School

Rotary Club President Rotarian Namrata Panicker, while congratulating the awardees, remarked, “The Nation Builder Award is a testimony to the immense dedication, hard work, and commitment that every teacher invests in shaping the future of our country.”
The event was seamlessly coordinated by Rotarian Dr. KD Gupta. Past President Rotarian Dr. Alok Mittal extended the vote of thanks, expressing gratitude to the teachers and attendees. Club Secretary Rotarian Er. Ashish Agarwal concluded the event by announcing the date of the next meeting.

Among the many notable Rotarians present were Rotarian Vinod Gupta, Rotarian Rajeev Lotchan Bharadwaj, Rotarian Ashish Agarwal, Rotarian Sunil Kapoor, Rotarian Vivek Gupta, Rotarian Manoj R. Kumar, Rotarian RS Mittal, Rotarian Shanti Swaroop Goyal, and Rotarian Vishnu Saran Mehra.

The Rotary Club of Agra continues to champion the vital role of educators in society, acknowledging their contributions to nation-building with admiration and respect.

activities.title: Workshop - Safe & Unsafe Touch - 1
activities.description:
September is celebrated by Rotary International as Basic Education and Literacy Month, and Rotary clubs around the world engage in numerous activities to promote this essential cause. Rotary Club of Agra is doing its part by addressing a critical issue that often goes unnoticed – the awareness of safe and unsafe touch, especially among schoolchildren. Recognizing this as an integral aspect of basic education, the club is committed to educating children about their rights to personal safety.
The club's President, Rotarian Namrata Panicker, emphasizes that understanding the concept of safe and unsafe touch should be woven into the very fabric of basic education. She advocates that this important subject be included in school curriculums, helping children identify inappropriate behaviour and protect themselves from potential harm. In light of this, Rotary Club of Agra has made it their mission to conduct workshops and awareness camps in schools, aiming to safeguard children from the dangers of sexual abuse.
In a significant step towards this goal, the club organized its first workshop at Kedarnath Sekhsariya Arya Kanya Inter College, Belanganj, Agra. The workshop featured Advocate Namrata Mishra, an expert in the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, as the keynote speaker. She provided valuable insights into how children can differentiate between safe and unsafe touch and offered practical advice on what to do if they ever experience such situations. The session proved to be a real eye-opener for the students, as it was the first time many of them had encountered such a candid discussion on this sensitive topic.
Advocate Mishra also shed light on the dangers posed by social media. She urged children to be cautious about sharing personal information online, highlighting how predators often take advantage of young minds' naivety to perpetrate online sexual abuse. Her message resonated strongly with the audience, underscoring the growing need to educate children not just about physical boundaries but also the digital threats they may face.
The workshop concluded with the school principal, Mrs. Namita Sharma, and Mrs. Neerja Sharma expressing their heartfelt thanks to the Rotary Club of Agra for addressing this crucial issue. They acknowledged the importance of such workshops in empowering students with the knowledge they need to protect themselves.
Several prominent Rotarians were present to support the initiative, including Rotarian Shailendra Nath Sharma, Rotarian Vinod Gupta, Rotarian Jitendra Jain, Rotarian Sunil Kapoor, Past President Rotarian Ashish Agarwal, and Rotarian Manoj R. Kumar. Their presence underscored the Rotary Club's commitment to making a lasting impact on children's safety and well-being in the community.
Through initiatives like these, Rotary Club of Agra is not only fulfilling its mission of basic education and literacy but also championing the cause of child protection and safety. With continued efforts, the club aims to inspire other educational institutions to adopt similar programs, ensuring that children everywhere are equipped with the knowledge to defend their rights and safeguard their futures.

activities.title: Safe Unsafe Touch & Poster Activity
activities.description:
Rotary Club of Agra Promotes Awareness on Safe and Unsafe Touch Among Schoolchildren

In a groundbreaking initiative, the Rotary Club of Agra has taken a crucial step toward addressing an issue that is often overlooked—raising awareness about safe and unsafe touch, especially among schoolchildren. Understanding this as a key element of basic education, the club is dedicated to teaching children about their right to personal safety and protection.

Rotary Club of Agra's President, Rotarian Namrata Panicker, stresses the importance of integrating this knowledge into school curriculums. She believes that helping children recognize inappropriate behavior and empowering them to protect themselves should be a fundamental part of their education. In light of this commitment, the club has made it their mission to organize workshops and awareness camps in schools, aiming to shield children from the threat of sexual abuse.

In a significant move, the club held its second workshop at Queen Victoria Girls’ Inter College, Hariparvat, Agra. Advocate Namrata Mishra, a specialist in the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, was the keynote speaker. She engaged the students by teaching them how to distinguish between safe and unsafe touch through storytelling. She further guided the children on how to react if they ever find themselves in uncomfortable or harmful situations. Advocate Mishra also led the students in taking a pledge to protect their bodies and to never allow anyone to touch them inappropriately.
In addition to physical safety, Advocate Mishra spoke about the increasing dangers of social media. She cautioned children about sharing personal information online, stressing that predators often exploit the innocence of young minds to commit online sexual abuse. Her message was clear: children must be vigilant not only about physical boundaries but also digital threats.

The workshop concluded with the school principal, Mrs. Joyce Sylas, expressing her gratitude to the Rotary Club of Agra for addressing such a vital issue. She emphasized the positive impact this session will have on the students' lives, helping them make informed decisions about their safety.

During this session awareness posters explaining safe-unsafe touch and important help line numbers that every child should know were also released in the school. Several prominent Rotarians, including Rotarian Shailendra Nath Sharma, Rotarian Vinod Gupta, Rotarian Jitendra Jain, Rotarian Richa Agarwal, and Rotarian Manoj R. Kumar, attended the event to show their support. Their presence highlighted the Rotary Club's commitment to creating lasting change in children's safety and well-being.

Through such initiatives, the Rotary Club of Agra is not only fulfilling its mission of advancing basic education and literacy but is also leading the charge in child protection. The club hopes that their continued efforts will inspire more schools and organizations to adopt similar programs, ensuring that children everywhere are empowered to safeguard their rights and futures.

activities.title: Nepal: Rotary Foundation Symposium Conference
activities.description:
Overview
The Rotary Consortium Conference was held in Kathmandu, Nepal, bringing together Rotarians from various districts to discuss and collaborate on key initiatives. The event featured a comprehensive agenda, including an inter-district tour, recognition of major donors, and a fellowship dinner.

Nepal Inter-District Tour
Participants embarked on an inter-district tour, visiting significant Rotary projects and local attractions. This tour provided an opportunity for Rotarians to witness the impact of their contributions firsthand and to exchange ideas on enhancing community service efforts.

Recognition of Major Donors
A special segment of the conference was dedicated to recognizing major donors who have contributed $10,000 or more to the Rotary International Fund. These generous contributions are crucial for supporting Rotary’s global initiatives, including health, education, and disaster relief programs. The donors were honored with certificates and plaques as a token of appreciation for their unwavering support.

Fellowship Dinner
The conference concluded with a fellowship dinner, fostering camaraderie among attendees. This dinner provided a relaxed environment for Rotarians to network, share experiences, and build stronger relationships. The evening was filled with engaging conversations, cultural performances, and a sense of unity and purpose.

Conclusion
The Rotary Consortium Conference in Kathmandu was a resounding success, highlighting the power of collaboration and generosity within the Rotary community. The inter-district tour, donor recognition, and fellowship dinner were key highlights that reinforced the commitment of Rotarians to making a positive impact worldwide.

activities.description:
Introduction
The Rotary Club, in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Kashipur, organized the Vikas 4.0 Entrepreneurial Course. This initiative aimed to enhance the business knowledge and entrepreneurial skills of young Rotarians. The course was designed to provide comprehensive training, mentorship, and practical insights into the world of business and entrepreneurship.

Objectives
1. Enhance Business Knowledge
2. Develop Entrepreneurial Skills
3. Provide Certification

The Vikas 4.0 course was structured to cover various aspects of business and entrepreneurship, including:

Business Management: 
Core principles of managing a business effectively.
Financial Acumen: Understanding financial statements, budgeting, and financial planning.
Marketing Strategies: Techniques for effective marketing and brand management.
Innovation and Design Thinking: Encouraging innovative thinking and problem-solving.
Leadership and Team Building: Developing leadership qualities and team management skills.

Key Highlights:
1. Expert Lectures
2. Interactive Workshops
3. Mentorship Program
4. Networking Opportunities

Outcomes
Enhanced Knowledge: Participants gained a deeper understanding of business operations and strategies.
Skill Development: Improved entrepreneurial skills, including critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making.
Certification: All participants received a certification from IIM Kashipur, recognizing their successful completion of the course.

Conclusion
The Vikas 4.0 Entrepreneurial Course was a significant step towards empowering young Rotarians with the knowledge and skills necessary to excel in the business world. The collaboration between the Rotary Club and IIM Kashipur provided a robust platform for learning and growth, ensuring that participants are well-equipped to take on entrepreneurial challenges.

activities.title: Workshop on Safe & Unsafe Touch - 3
activities.description:
The Rotary Club of Agra has taken a vital initiative to address a critical issue that is often overlooked—educating schoolchildren about safe and unsafe touch. In a world where personal safety is paramount, the club is committed to raising awareness on this subject as an essential part of basic education, ensuring children understand their right to protection and personal safety.
Rotary Club of Agra President, Rotarian Namrata Panicker, emphasized the need for integrating such knowledge into school curriculums. "Empowering children to recognize inappropriate behavior and safeguarding themselves should be a fundamental part of their education," she stated. As part of this mission, the club has been organizing workshops and awareness camps across schools to protect children from the dangers of sexual abuse.
In a significant step forward, the club recently conducted its second workshop at Smt. BD Jain Girls' Inter College, Agra Cantt. The keynote speaker, Advocate Namrata Mishra, a specialist in the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, led an engaging session aimed at helping students distinguish between safe and unsafe touch through storytelling. She also provided practical advice on how to respond if they ever find themselves in uncomfortable or harmful situations. Advocate Mishra guided the students in taking a pledge to protect their bodies and to reject any form of inappropriate contact.
Advocate Mishra also addressed the increasing dangers posed by social media. She warned students against sharing personal information online, explaining that predators often exploit the innocence of children to engage in online sexual abuse. Her message was clear: children must be aware not only of physical boundaries but also of the risks in the digital world.
The workshop saw the participation of over 400 students and concluded with a message of gratitude from the school principal – Smt. Anjali Nakra. She thanked the Rotary Club of Agra for shedding light on such an important issue, noting the lasting impact the session would have on students' ability to make informed decisions about their safety.
Additionally, the workshop featured the release of awareness posters explaining the differences between safe and unsafe touch, along with important helpline numbers every child should know. Rotarian Manoj R. Kumar oversaw the event's arrangements, ensuring the success of the program.
With efforts like these, the Rotary Club of Agra is playing a pivotal role in equipping children with the tools they need to stay safe, both in the real world and online.

activities.title: Cervical Cancer Vaccination Program
activities.description:
The Rotary Club of Agra successfully administered the third dose of the free cervical cancer vaccine to 60 girls from Srimati B.D. Jain Girls PG College, Agra Cantt. The event took place in the presence of the Honorable Mayor of Agra, Smt. Hemlata Diwaker, who served as the chief guest.
The program began with the traditional lighting of the lamp by the dignitaries. Dr. Surabhi Gupta, Head of the Department of Radiation Oncology at SN Medical College, Agra, and the keynote speaker for the event, addressed the students on the importance of vaccination. She highlighted that the cervical cancer vaccine not only reduces the risk of developing the disease but also offers protection against several other related health issues. Dr. Gupta further clarified the misconception that the vaccine is only for females, stating that it is equally beneficial for males, and that many parents have started vaccinating their sons as well.
The vaccination drive was conducted through Help Agra.
Rotary Club of Agra President, Rotarian Namrata Panicker, emphasized the club’s commitment to health initiatives. She remarked that just as Rotary played a pivotal role in eradicating polio through widespread vaccination, the club is now focused on promoting cervical cancer vaccination on a larger scale.
Chief Guest Smt. Hemlata Diwaker, an alumna of Srimati B.D. Jain Girls PG College, praised the government’s dedication to public health and well-being. She commended the Rotary Club of Agra for its significant contributions to the community, particularly in healthcare.
During the event, senior Rotarian Ram Saran Mittal was honored for sponsoring the entire vaccination program.
Prof. Vandana Agarwal, Principal of Srimati B.D. Jain Girls PG College, expressed her heartfelt gratitude to the Rotary Club of Agra for vaccinating the students and safeguarding them against this serious illness.
The event was also graced by the presence of several Rotarians, including Secretary Rotarian Er. Ashish Agarwal, Rotarian SK Jain, Rotarian Rajeev Lotchan Bharadwaj, Rotarian Rajesh Jain, Rotarian Shailendra Nath Sharma, and Rotarian Manoj R Kumar.

activities.title: Seminar on Destination Marketing in Tourism
activities.description:
The Rotary Club of Agra, in collaboration with Sharda University, Agra, organized a seminar on "Destination Marketing in Tourism" today, in celebration of World Tourism Day. The event featured Professor Dr. Jayanthi Ranjan, Vice Chancellor of Sharda University, as the Chief Guest, and District Governor Rotarian Neerav Nimesh Agarwal as the Guest of Honour. The program commenced with a traditional lamp lighting ceremony and Saraswati Vandana, performed by the distinguished guests.
Professor Lavkush Mishra from the Institute of Tourism & Hotel Management at Dr. B.R. Ambedkar University delivered an insightful talk on the topic. He emphasized the significance of city names in destination marketing, noting that these names often reflect a city's cultural heritage. He also highlighted the irony of how the West is now adopting ancient Indian cultural practices that were originally rooted in scientific reasoning.
Shri Hari Sukumar, Vice President of Operations at Jaypee Hotel & Convention Centre, Agra, and keynote speaker for the seminar, discussed Agra’s untapped tourism potential beyond the Taj Mahal. He pointed out that historical sites like Chinni Ka Roza and Mariam’s Tomb are under-promoted, and if marketed effectively, Agra could offer tourists a richer, multi-day experience, thereby boosting the city's economy.
District Governor Rotarian Neerav Nimesh Agarwal elaborated on the importance of holistic destination marketing, using Agra and Mathura as examples. He highlighted that while Agra primarily promotes the Taj Mahal, Mathura successfully markets its cultural and traditional attractions, resulting in a higher tourist influx.
Rotary coordinator Rotarian Sharat Chandra underscored the role of youth in driving societal change and emphasized the Rotary's efforts to engage young people through Rotaract Clubs, fostering future leaders who contribute positively to society.
Club President and event co-host, Rotarian Namrata Panicker, emphasized the interconnectedness of tourism with other industries, noting that tourism growth can significantly uplift the economy. She also highlighted Rotary's role in promoting tourism on a global scale through international student exchange and friendship programs.
Chief Guest, Professor Dr. Jayanthi Ranjan, expressed her gratitude to the Rotary Club for partnering with Sharda University for this enriching event. She reaffirmed the university's commitment to inclusive education and stressed the importance of connecting students with their cultural roots, while also outlining various initiatives the university is undertaking.
A drawing and painting competition on the theme of tourism was also organized for students, with winners being honored during the seminar.
The event was hosted by CA Sanjeev Thakur and attended by notable guests including Professor Dr. Sachin Srivastava, Rotarian Vinod Gupta, Rotarian Ashish Agarwal, Rotarian Manoj R. Kumar, Rotarian Sonal Agarwal, Rotarian Rajeev Lochan Bharadwaj, Rotarian Ashutosh Kumar, Past President Rotarian Ashish Agarwal, and several other prominent Rotarians and dignitaries. Vote of thanks was given by Shri Atul Narang.
